data: 367 kg launch mass; 1.2 kW solar-electric Hall-effect ion thruster
Public domain / ESA archive. First European spacecraft to reach the Moon; first mission to reach the Moon under ion propulsion.
NSSDCA Master Catalog, SMART-1 (2003-043C) mission profile

Kourou, 2003-09-27 23:14 UT, as an auxiliary passenger on Ariane 5. SMART-1 is released into a ~742 x 36,016 km geostationary transfer orbit, inclined 7 degrees, and begins its ion-engine spiral to the Moon.
After lunar resonance manoeuvres in August, September and October 2004, a final 100-hour continuous ion-engine thrust arc (10-14 October 2004) lifts the apogee to the Moon's distance.
2004-11-13. The Moon's gravity captures SMART-1 at about 60,000 km from the lunar surface, after the spacecraft passed the Earth-Moon L1 region.
Ion engine fires to lower lunar orbit
2004-11-15 05:24 UT. The ion engine starts a 4.5-day thrust period to lower the orbit from the initial 4,962 x 51,477 km, 81-degree capture orbit toward a 300 x 3,000 km polar orbit.
2004-11-15 17:48 UT. SMART-1 passes its first perilune about 5,000 km above the surface; ESA marks 15 November 2004 as arrival in lunar orbit, 415 days after launch.
First European spacecraft to reach the Moon; first mission to reach the Moon under ion propulsion

ESA's first lunar mission and the first European spacecraft to reach the Moon. SMART = Small Missions for Advanced Research in Technology — and the key technology was a Hall-effect solar-electric ion thruster (PPS-1350-G), at the time the largest such thruster ever flown. Launched 2003-09-27 as a shared payload on an Ariane 5 from Kourou, the 367-kg spacecraft used its 1.2-kW xenon ion drive over 13 months to slowly raise its Earth orbit, eventually captured by lunar gravity on 2004-11-15 — a 13-month low-thrust spiral rather than the usual days-long chemical transfer. Operated for about 22 months in a polar lunar orbit returning AMIE camera imagery, X-ray fluorescence elemental maps of the Moon (D-CIXS), and infrared mineral spectroscopy (SIR). Deliberately impacted Lacus Excellentiae (34.4° S, 46.2° W) on 2006-09-03 05:42 UTC — the impact flash was observed live from the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope.
Ariane 5G from Kourou 2003-09-27 23:14 UTC — shared payload with Insat-3E + e-Bird.
PPS-1350-G Hall-effect ion thruster begins 13-month low-thrust spiral.
Captured by lunar gravity 2004-11-15 — first European spacecraft at the Moon.
D-CIXS X-ray fluorescence delivers elemental maps of the Moon.
Deliberate impact at 34.4° S, 46.2° W on 2006-09-03 05:42 UTC. Impact flash observed from CFHT.
